solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Location for Burning Man spotted around mountain range

parts.note: a pyre is the heap on which a body is burned

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so the word is read back to front

parts.note: spotted means seen

explanation.surface: Directions to the Nevada desert festival Burning Man, glimpsed somewhere near a range of mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: Burning Man looks like the name of the festival, but it is read literally: the place where a man is burned is a pyre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the chain of peaks along the border between France and Spain.

clue.text: Very valuable publicity? Neat!

parts.note: PR is public relations, i.e. publicity
a neat drink is served without ice

explanation.surface: Someone delighted at a burst of free publicity, exclaiming how neat it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat!' reads as an exclamation of approval, but it is the barman's sense: a spirit poured straight, with no ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so valuable that no sum could buy it is beyond price.

clue.text: Team gets irritated following striker's finish

indicators.note: to follow is to come behind, so this part is placed after the other
a finish is the end of something, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of striker
anger used intransitively: someone who angers easily gets irritated easily

explanation.surface: A football side loses its temper after their centre forward finishes, or fails to.
explanation.walkthrough: Anger can be intransitive, as in 'he angers quickly', which lets the verb mean gets irritated. Rangers are a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is the name of a well-known Scottish football club, a team based in Glasgow.

clue.text: Fool returning home with another

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: at home is in
another word for a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot coming back to the house bringing a second idiot along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another fool, so it borrows its sense from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly, foolish person, a mild insult for someone lacking sense.

clue.text: Hard to find gripping 90's newspaper article

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it tight, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: something elusive is hard to find
XC is 90 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A gripping story from a 1990s newspaper that is now hard to track down.
explanation.walkthrough: '90's' looks like a decade; it is the number 90 in Roman numerals, and the 's is just the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive is a story published by only one paper, a scoop no rival carried.

clue.text: Film hero shunning Ben catches steamship with a soldier

indicators.note: to catch is to take hold of, so one piece is held inside another
to shun is to avoid or keep away, so those letters are left out

parts.note: Ben-Hur is the title hero of the 1959 chariot-race epic
the part of the name that is dropped
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A movie hero avoiding someone called Ben and boarding a steamer with an army companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing BEN from BENHUR leaves HUR, which then holds SS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalry soldier, originally from Hungary, known for flamboyant uniforms.

clue.text: Detestable European stopping collection for a busker?

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so this piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a street performer collects coins in an upturned hat
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A nasty foreigner interrupting the coins thrown to a street musician.
explanation.walkthrough: A busker is a street performer who passes the hat round, so a hatful is what they collect.
explanation.definitionFit: Hateful and detestable are synonyms, both describing something that arouses strong loathing.

clue.text: Sandwich consumed after pitcher put down

indicators.note: after means coming later, so this part is placed behind the one before it

parts.note: a sub is a long filled roll
a pitcher is a jug
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A sandwich eaten after a baseball pitcher is taken out of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitcher suggests baseball, which suits the American sub, but here it is a jug for pouring.
explanation.definitionFit: To subjugate is to conquer and bring under control, much as a rebellion is crushed.

clue.text: Pet also pummelled Peter, perhaps

indicators.note: something pummelled is beaten out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog or cat that also gave someone named Peter a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter reads as the victim of the pummelling, but he is the definition, with 'perhaps' showing he is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Peter was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus, so he is an example.

clue.text: One working to get B+ in chemistry, say

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A student studying hard to earn a B-plus grade in their chemistry exam.
explanation.walkthrough: B+ looks like a school grade; in chemistry it is a boron atom carrying a positive charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A charged atom such as positively charged boron is a cation, one kind of electrically charged particle.

clue.text: Pass close to celebrity and express disapproval well

parts.note: a pass that admits you is a ticket

indicators.note: the close of something is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of celebrity
to boo is to jeer

explanation.surface: Walking right past a celebrity and showing clear disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' sits at the end looking like an adverb for how the disapproval is expressed; it is the definition, meaning fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickety-boo is old-fashioned British slang for everything being fine and in good order.

clue.text: Retired? Put it in new resume

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the letters come out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a retiree to mention their retirement on an updated CV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put ... in' looks like an insertion, but the inserted word joins the anagram fodder before anything is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a professor or official who has retired but keeps their title as an honour.

clue.text: Just missing out on bronze and uranium in river

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river flowing into the Firth of Forth
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: An athlete narrowly failing to take third place, with a stray radioactive element in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the long phrase at the front: the place just outside the medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronze goes to third place, so the next finisher misses a medal by one position.

clue.text: Point of banquet not having starter

indicators.note: the starter is the first thing served, so without it the opening letter is gone

parts.note: a banquet is a feast

explanation.surface: Asking what a banquet is for if there is no first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter fits the banquet as the first course, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal compass points, so it is a point of direction.

clue.text: Poet right to change line, for balance

indicators.note: to change these letters is to alter their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet entitled to alter one line of verse so the stanza is balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: Line looks like a line of poetry; it is a rope, on which an acrobat keeps their balance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope is a taut wire or cord stretched high, along which performers walk balancing.

clue.text: Mastermind of heavy metal band, originally, then Queen

indicators.note: originally means at first, then means next, so these words fix the order of the parts

parts.note: a band, such as a wedding band, is a ring
lead is a heavy metal
ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: The brains behind a heavy metal group who later formed the rock band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: A heavy metal band is read as a band made of heavy metal, a lead ring, whose two parts come in the order RING then LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader is the person who organises and directs a group, especially in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Resentment with stock market debut — large one — in part of Turkey

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the pieces join up end to end

parts.note: gall is bitterness or resentment
an IPO, initial public offering, is a company's first listing
L is the abbreviation for large
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Bitterness in Turkey over a big stock flotation.
explanation.walkthrough: IPO stands for initial public offering, when a company's shares are first sold to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli is a peninsula in north-west Turkey, site of the 1915 campaign.

clue.text: Musical recap, OK or terrible?

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic asking whether a summary of a stage musical was acceptable or awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' sits up front like an adjective describing the recap, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock opera, such as Tommy, is a stage or recorded musical work set to rock music.

clue.text: Bug nearly put on band member in recital

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to put on a play is to stage it

indicators.note: a recital is a performance spoken or sung aloud, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a member of the Beatles, the Liverpool band

explanation.surface: An insect almost getting the better of a musician during a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' suggests placing one thing beside another, but it is the theatrical sense, to mount a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The stag beetle is a large insect whose males have huge antler-like jaws.

clue.text: Movement of time went quickly with model

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the pieces join up end to end

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ran means went quickly
an artist's model sits for them

explanation.surface: Time flew past while someone was in the company of a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: Model looks like a noun but is the verb: to model for a painter is to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the conveying or passage of people or goods from one place to another.

clue.text: Make secret cell beneath church supporting essence of Lent

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath the other
the essence of something is its core, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of Lent
a crypt is an underground chamber below a church

explanation.surface: Hiding away in a chamber under a church to observe the true spirit of Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the supporting piece goes below, so the Lent letters sit above the church vault.
explanation.definitionFit: To encrypt is to convert information into a code so that outsiders cannot read it.

clue.text: Help witch periodically? It's a long story

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Someone asking how they can assist a witch now and then, and being told it would take ages to explain.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of the two words together gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem or tale of heroic deeds, like the Iliad.

clue.text: Friend to declare carry-on

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A friend at the airport needing to declare items from their hand luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry-on suggests cabin baggage; in British usage a carry-on is a fuss or commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver means a tedious fuss or bother, the same sense as a carry-on.

clue.text: Beginning of solution to stuffy room announced

indicators.note: something announced is said out loud, so the answer is how the words sound

parts.note: the fix for a stuffy room is to put in an air vent

explanation.surface: The first step in fixing a room with no fresh air, as stated out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning of' suggests taking a first letter; instead Beginning is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival or coming into being, the start of something new.

clue.text: Curry gets cold, very cold

parts.note: a balti is a curry cooked and served in a metal bowl, popular in Birmingham
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A takeaway curry left to go cold, then freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: Baltic for freezing weather is informal British slang, from the chilly Baltic Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, weather described as Baltic is bitterly, freezingly cold.

clue.text: After French wine, drink ale at first then head for spicy meal

indicators.note: after means following, so this part comes behind the rest

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: at first points to the opening, so only initial letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of both words
the head is a ship's toilet, as is a loo

explanation.surface: A night out: wine, then beer, then off to the curry house for something hot.
explanation.walkthrough: Head is naval slang for a toilet, so it gives LOO, the British word for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A vindaloo is a fiercely hot curry of Goan origin, a byword for spiciness.

clue.text: Without any green entry books, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters fall into disarray

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An accountant regretting that the ledgers contain no green-ink entries at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Green is slang for money, from the colour of dollar bills, so 'without any green' means penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony-broke is British slang for completely penniless, having no money whatsoever.

clue.text: Awful to forget Liberal struggle

indicators.note: to forget something is to leave it out, so that letter goes

parts.note: vile means awful
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A political lament that it is dreadful to overlook the Liberals' fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberal with a capital looks like the party, but it is just the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete or contend with rivals, the same as to struggle for something.

clue.text: Ignore this covering on road

indicators.note: a covering goes around what it covers, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to ignore a correction
re means on, as in concerning

explanation.surface: An instruction to disregard the surface material laid on a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignore this' reads as an aside to the solver but is the editorial instruction stet, Latin for let it stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a public road in a town, usually with buildings along its sides.

clue.text: Mostly icy mountain cuts through Australian state

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: via means by way of, through

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A frozen peak slicing across one of Australia's states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Through' looks like part of 'cuts through', but it is the word VIA, which the other letters split.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is the south-eastern Australian state whose capital is Melbourne.
